what: First controller pass over the rebuilt AI models screen
verdict: FAILED - the screen cannot be operated with a controller

where.build: the plan 62 build, deployed by the maintainer
where.build_confirmed_by: the models list rule read off the running page shows this session's fix (fill the popup body, no screen-share cap), and the Filters row, the Advanced link and the by-hand name chip are all present
where.screen_in_use: external 1920x1080 monitor, reported to the page as 1500x843 at 1.28 device pixels per drawing pixel
where.game_running: none - the panel read 'Context: no active game detected' and no game process was running

how_the_screen_was_opened: Ollama tab, then the Browse models button in Where AI runs. Two presses down from the Advanced link reaches the Filters button, so the Filters button itself is reachable.

the_failure.what_a_person_would_see: Pressing A on the Filters button closes the whole AI models screen. The filters never appear. Pressing A on a model's tick box also closes the whole screen, so no model can be ticked to download.

reproduced.advanced_link: twice, worked correctly both times - the screen stayed open and switched to the Advanced view

readings_after_the_press.where_the_highlight_went: back to the Browse models button in the plugin panel, which is the normal path when the screen closes

the_failure.so_it_closed_cleanly_rather_than_crashed: The highlight returning to the button that opened it is the screen's own closing behaviour, so this is a close, not a crash.

cause.mechanism: The screen is a confirm-style dialog whose OK action closes it. A press of A that no control claims reaches that OK, so the screen closes. The React-level stopPropagation these controls already call does not stop Steam's own gamepad press, which travels a different path.
cause.the_proof_is_the_one_control_that_works: The Advanced link is the only control on the screen that carries an explicit gamepad OK handler calling stopPropagation, and it is the only control that behaves correctly.
controls_missing_that_handler: Type a model name by hand
Close typing a model name by hand
every cell in the model table, including each row's tick box and Remove from Deck

row_count_measured_anyway.note: The row count this row also asks for was read before the failure was found, with the maintainer's own filters as they were set.
row_count_measured_anyway.what_this_means: With Essentials only switched on, the list is short enough that nothing needs scrolling at all, so the height is not what limits the count here - the filter is. The count with the full catalogue could not be measured, because turning Essentials only off needs the Filters panel, which is what cannot be opened.
row_count_measured_anyway.the_height_cap_is_gone: The list rule on the running build reads 'fill the popup body' with no screen-share cap, so this session's height fix is live on the device.

not_reached_because_of_the_failure: Whether the D-pad can get back out of the Filters panel.
Whether each of the six filters changes the list.
Whether the licence filter does what the three old Policy buttons did.
Whether B closes the by-hand name box or the whole screen.

deck_left_as_found.ask_model_untouched: A was never pressed on the 'Use for Ask' cell - the highlight was moved past it deliberately
